title: UV/H 2 O 2  treatment of hotpot-seasoning biological tailwater: organic removal and biological effect-based effluent safety assessment
content: Advanced oxidation processes are widely used as polishing treatments for biologically treated industrial wastewater, but the biological effects of treated effluents remain insufficiently understood. This study investigated the treatment performance of a UV/H2O2 system for hotpot-seasoning biological tailwater and its effects on the green alga Tetradesmus obliquus. At an H2O2 dosage of 1 mM and a reaction time of 60 min, the total organic carbon (TOC) and UV254 removal reached 78.5% and 86.4%, respectively, mainly through a hydroxyl radical-mediated reactions. Although the process improved the chemical quality, the treated effluent weakened the growth-promoting effect of the original biological tailwater and reduced algal biomass, chlorophyll, protein, and carbohydrate contents, while increasing the carotenoid content. These results indicate that chemical removal does not necessarily correspond to reduced biological effects. Transcriptomic and non-targeted metabolomic analyses were further used to interpret the algal responses induced by the treated effluent. The affected pathways were mainly associated with photosynthesis, energy metabolism, nitrogen assimilation, aminoacyl-tRNA biosynthesis, carbon metabolism, and biological macromolecule accumulation. Overall, this study shows that green algae-based biological effect assessment can provide additional information for evaluating AOP-treated industrial effluents and may help support the optimization of polishing processes for food industry wastewater.
